android.desc:
Transfer photos, videos, music, documents and folders from your Android phone or tablet to a PC, NAS or server. No USB cable needed. Choose quick QR code sharing over Wi-Fi or connect using SMB, SFTP and FTP.

Quick QR code sharing
Select the files you want to share and start QR sharing. Scan the code with another device on the same Wi-Fi network, or open the displayed address in its web browser to download the files. No SMB, SFTP or FTP configuration is needed for QR sharing.

Transfer to PC, NAS or server
Use SMB to access Windows shared folders and compatible NAS storage. Use SFTP or FTP to connect to supported servers on your local network or over the internet when the server is reachable.

Back up and manage files
• Copy photos, videos, music, documents and other Android files to your chosen destination.
• Select individual files, whole folders or specific file types.
• Skip files that already exist at the destination during repeated transfers and backups.
• Optionally delete copied files from your Android device after a successful transfer to free up space.

Two ways to transfer
Use QR code sharing for quick downloads to another device with a browser. Choose SMB, SFTP or FTP for regular transfers to a computer, NAS or server. Files To Computer puts wireless file transfer, backup and QR sharing in one app.

quotes.text:
In general, people just use noIP home router VPN, ssh/sftp host on LAN, and a sshfs client on their iOS/Android device or MacOS/Windows/Linux.  It will look like any other network shared drive in the native OS.

For paid services, there are also native Dropbox client support in MATE, Ubuntu, or Mint desktop file managers etc.

iOS sftp:

https://www.photosync-app.com/home

Android sftp:

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=cz.bukacek.filestocomputer&hl=en_CA

Practically speaking, I often recommend dual booting from 2 ssd drives for windows and Linux.   There are just some commercial software/games that can't run properly within a linux environment (programs like Wine do allow running some Windows native programs, but YMMV.)

https://www.linuxmint.com/  or https://ubuntu.com/download/desktop  is a great starter OS.

If you already use a posix system like MacOS, than the workflow will seem more familiar. =3

quotes.text:
SSH File sync applications are reliable...

Android: "Transfer Files To Computer, PC" ( Michal Bukáček includes GPL git URI, YMMV as we still need to audit it for traffic)

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=cz.bukacek.filestocomputer

iPhone: PhotoSync is free to transfer movies and low-resolution images

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/photosync-transfer-photos/id415850124

MacOS:

https://github.com/macfuse/macfuse/releases

Windows 11: sshfs is slow, but allows user account constrained access to remote shares

winget install -h -e --id "WinFsp.WinFsp"

winget install -h -e --id "SSHFS-Win.SSHFS-Win"

https://github.com/winfsp/sshfs-win

Windows 11 system tray sshfs link manager:

https://github.com/evsar3/sshfs-win-manager

Windows 11: Local OpenSSH service setup

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/openssh/openssh_install_firstuse

If your home router is dynamic DNS only, the ISP will usually still support ports >1000:

https://www.noip.com/

Or DIY with your own DNS solution with cloudflare:

https://linuxconfig.org/automate-dynamic-ip-updates-for-your-domain-with-cloudflare-and-bash-script

Also tried KDE connect a few years back, but didn't like the idea of giving a buggy phone access to shoulder-surf root accounts.  Transferring stuff out of a VM with a local samba instance also works, but samba should also be containerized.

Best regards, =3

quotes.text:
On windows, no one should be running SMB either.

There are network mount options (also include ssh support)

https://rclone.org/install/

And SSH access and remote IFS NFS drive mount to host with winget:

# Run PowerShell as an Administrator.

Get-WindowsCapability -Online | Where-Object Name -like 'OpenSSH*'

# Install the OpenSSH Client

Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Client~~~~0.0.1.0

# Install the OpenSSH Server

Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Server~~~~0.0.1.0

Start-Service sshd

Set-Service -Name sshd -StartupType 'Automatic'

# Only allow local or VPN host server access

New-NetFirewallRule -Name sshd -DisplayName 'OpenSSH Server (sshd)' -Enabled True -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -Action Allow -LocalPort 22 -RemoteAddress 192.168.1.0/24

winget install frequency403.OpenSSHGUI

winget install -h -e --id "WinFsp.WinFsp"

winget install -h -e --id "SSHFS-Win.SSHFS-Win"

winget install -h -e evsar3.sshfs-win-manager

#As administrator in power shell run to manage ssh keys:

OpenSSH-GUI-win-x64

And free/paid apps for your phone to sync your files automatically over SFTP.

https://filezilla-project.org/download.php?show_all=1

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=cz.bukacek.filestocomputer

https://apps.apple.com/ca/app/photosync-transfer-photos/id415850124

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.touchbyte.photosync

Stop using SMB, it was always broken on Windows and Linux. =3
